thread:
rob_acme: Hey team — our POC started getting a flurry of 5xx / 503s when we ramp to ~120 rps. Demo in 24h, can we triage? Logs: https://logs.redwood.acme/poc/trace/abc123
maria_se: pinging @alex_support and ops. Can you paste a sample request id and region?
alex_support: looking now. Seen a burst of 503 returning from the swarm layer — seems capacity fallback didn't handoff to burstpool immediately. grabbing logs.
deploy-bot: Autoscaler: scale-up requested for pool dedicated-acme at 12:43:10 UTC, provisioning 2 nodes (ETA ~60s)
rob_acme: example request ids: rq_20260321_01, rq_20260321_02. region: us-west-2. Model: gpt-open-8k-q (pinned)
sean_ops: checked infra logs — queue length spiked to 800, average service time ~120ms. Rate limiter started rejecting after queue>500. Also see errors: "KV cache OOM" and "fallback_incompatible_variant"
rob_acme: here's our route config:
```
route: /generate
model: gpt-open-8k-q
fallback_policy:
  - type: burstpool
    max_wait_ms: 2000
    burstpool_count: 0
```
ingrid_platform: important: you've pinned to the quantized variant only. our fallback pool currently has non-quantized variants — that's why "fallback_incompatible_variant" appears. The router will skip fallback if variants mismatch.
maria_se: quick pricing Q: will enabling burstpool add additional charges for the POC?
pm_jordan: yes — burstpool incurs reserved instance billing while active. For a short demo we can enable 1 extra burst node, estimate ~$150/day for the POC (rough ballpark).
alex_support: immediate mitigation options:
1) temporarily unpin model (allow compatible variant fallback)
2) increase burstpool_count to 1 or 2
3) add a soft QPS cap from client side to smooth ramp
we can push a canary with (1)+(2) in ~10-15m.
rob_acme: we can try unpinning. How do we toggle quickly?
alex_support: toggle is in console under route config -> uncheck "pin variant" or via API:
```
PATCH /v1/routes/{route_id}
{ "model_variant_policy": "allow_compatible" }
```
sean_ops: also recommend increasing autoscaler cooldown to avoid oscillation and set min_capacity=1 for the burstpool during the demo.
ingrid_platform: note that autoscale provisioning still has ~45-90s cold start on some AZs; fallback expected behavior is to hand off to burstpool if configured and compatible. Right now burstpool_count=0 so nothing to hand off to.
rob_acme: switched burstpool_count to 1 and unpinned the variant. Doing another ramp.
deploy-bot: Config change applied by alex_support at 12:56:40 UTC: burstpool_count=1, model_variant_policy=allow_compatible
rob_acme: quick update — error rate dropped by ~80% during the next ramp. Still seeing occasional 503s during 2m windows.
maria_se: thanks — that's promising. For the demo we may need docs of the fix to show to customer — can we get a short playbook?
alex_support: I'll write a brief playbook in the ticket and link it. Short version: unpin -> enable burstpool -> increase min_capacity -> apply client-side ramp. We'll also collect traces for postmortem. :thumbsup:
sean_ops: save these trace ids and queue dumps: rq_20260321_01, rq_20260321_02, rq_20260321_07. we'll run deeper analysis post-demo.
rob_acme: thanks team — demo in ~22h now. will report if anything else pops. Appreciate the fast turnaround :pray:
ingrid_platform: follow-up action: we'll schedule a short postmortem and recommend permanent config for dedicated POCs (min_capacity and compatible variants).
pm_jordan: noted on billing, will email acme estimate. 
alex_support: marking this thread for follow-up. If errors recur tag me and @sean_ops.
rob_acme: ack. thanks everyone.
